content.text:
Yes. Entire now supports `git-refs`, and switching does not rewrite your Git history or discard checkpoint history.

For JSHack specifically:

- Current state: 675 legacy checkpoints on `entire/checkpoints/v1`; no per-checkpoint refs locally.
- New checkpoints can use refs with:

```bash
entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs --project
```

- Existing branch checkpoints remain readable as legacy history; they are not automatically erased. Entire’s current design routes newer checkpoints through refs and older hex-ID checkpoints through the legacy branch. [Entire checkpoint storage docs](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/files/docs/architecture/release-origins.md)
- Your installed CLI is `0.10.2`; it supports the switch but does not expose the newer `entire checkpoint migrate` command. So this would be a “switch future checkpoints, preserve old branch” migration—not a conversion of all 675 records into refs.

I would recommend switching to refs and retaining `entire/checkpoints/v1` indefinitely for backward compatibility. We should first push the two currently unpushed checkpoints, then change the project setting and verify a new checkpoint lands under `refs/entire/checkpoints/...`.
Honestly - once we're converted to refs, why would we keep the old checkpoint branch laying around? (certainly on the remote) -- but I dont mind hanging onto it locally.

You’re right. Once every legacy checkpoint has been copied and verified as an individual `refs/entire/checkpoints/...` ref, the remote `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch has no ongoing value.

The only reasons to retain it remotely are:

- rollback insurance during migration;
- compatibility with older Entire clients;
- preserving legacy checkpoints that were not converted.

So the ideal end state is:

1. Convert all 675 branch checkpoints to refs.
2. Verify representative old and recent checkpoints with `entire explain`.
3. Switch the project backend to `refs`.
4. Keep the branch locally if desired.
5. Delete only the remote branch.

The important distinction is that `entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs` alone does not convert the existing branch history. With this installed `0.10.2` CLI, the migration command is not available, so deleting the remote branch immediately would make the old checkpoint history inaccessible remotely. Newer Entire releases have a dedicated checkpoint migration workflow for this conversion. [Entire’s ref-storage design](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/files/docs/architecture/release-origins.md) supports legacy branch reads during the transition.

So: yes, delete it remotely after conversion; retain it locally as a cheap safety net.
